accessClasses.label: Public ordinary-app route
accessClasses.definition: Callable by an ordinary application through supported Android APIs on the tested build.

accessClasses.label: Hidden or vendor-callable candidate
accessClasses.definition: A hidden or vendor interface may be callable without system-camera identity, but the exact route has not been reproduced.

accessClasses.label: Privileged/system application route
accessClasses.definition: Requires caller eligibility beyond an ordinary application, such as SYSTEM_CAMERA plus associated package policy.

accessClasses.label: Rooted or custom-ROM route
accessClasses.definition: Requires policy, filesystem, service, or firmware changes outside the ordinary application sandbox.

accessClasses.label: Firmware-internal route
accessClasses.definition: Implemented inside provider, HAL, ISP, tuning, or native firmware components with no verified application contract.

layers.label: Package identity, grants, roles, and allowlists

galaga-expert-route.supports: Stock Galaga manual configuration maps 0.6x to ID 2, 1x to ID 0, and 2x through 10x to ID 3.

authorization-comparison.supports: Defines package permission, AppOps, allowlist, UID, install partition, and SELinux comparison gates without assuming successful endpoint access.

system-camera-filtering.supports: IDs 2 through 5 are omitted from ordinary enumeration and rejected at characteristics as system-only; connect is not independently reached by the current probe.

camera-error-taxonomy.supports: Separates characteristics, open preflight, connect, session, and request failures and preserves API-specific error namespaces.

system-camera-contract.supports: Documents the AOSP system-camera contract and target-aligned rejection vocabulary.

public-camera-baseline.supports: Public IDs 0 and 1 are listed, readable, and openable by the ordinary diagnostic application.

deploymentClasses.label: Ordinary public application
deploymentClasses.consequence: Ship only public routes and independently reproduced vendor routes; keep system-camera backends fail-closed.

deploymentClasses.label: Legitimate OEM/system deployment
deploymentClasses.consequence: Requires an authorized package identity, grants, allowlists, roles, AppOps, and matching SELinux/service policy.

deploymentClasses.label: Rooted or custom-ROM integration
deploymentClasses.consequence: Implement as a separate backend with explicit installation, policy, compatibility, and recovery requirements.

deploymentClasses.label: Stock-camera handoff
deploymentClasses.consequence: Can invoke the official app but does not provide in-process frame access or constitute a complete replacement.

features.label: Public rear main capture

firstBoundary.reason: The ordinary diagnostic application enumerates, reads, and opens ID 0.

features.replacementConsequence: Implement in the ordinary Camera2 backend and expose as a real optical wide route.

features.label: Public digital zoom

firstBoundary.reason: Public zoom remains on ID 0 and is a crop, not an auxiliary optical route.

features.replacementConsequence: Label the result as digital zoom and never substitute it while reporting an optical ultrawide or telephoto route.

features.label: Direct ultrawide endpoint

firstBoundary.reason: The endpoint is omitted from the ordinary caller camera list and status visibility.

features.replacementConsequence: Keep the Galaga auxiliary backend fail-closed in ordinary builds; enable only after an independent lawful authorization probe succeeds.

hardRejection.reason: The ordinary caller receives the exact system-only-device rejection before connection.

features.label: Direct telephoto endpoint

firstBoundary.reason: The endpoint is omitted from the ordinary caller camera list and status visibility.

features.replacementConsequence: Keep the Galaga auxiliary backend fail-closed in ordinary builds; enable only after an independent lawful authorization probe succeeds.

hardRejection.reason: The ordinary caller receives the exact system-only-device rejection before connection.

features.label: System SAT/logical endpoint

firstBoundary.reason: The endpoint is omitted from the ordinary caller camera list and status visibility.

features.replacementConsequence: Do not route ordinary captures through ID 4 or present it as available until its role and authorization are independently reproduced.

hardRejection.reason: ID 4 is recognized as system-only for the ordinary caller; its precise stock-mode role remains unresolved.

features.label: System portrait/composite endpoint

firstBoundary.reason: The endpoint is omitted from the ordinary caller camera list and status visibility.

features.replacementConsequence: Treat portrait/composite access as unavailable in the ordinary backend until both role and authorization are reproduced.

hardRejection.reason: ID 5 is recognized as system-only for the ordinary caller; its precise composition role remains unresolved.

features.label: Public-ID vendor/session routing candidate
features.route: ID 0 plus MediaTek/Nothing session or request state

firstBoundary.reason: Vendor session, request, and physical-output mechanisms exist, but no exact ordinary-callable route has been reproduced.

features.replacementConsequence: Research only exact typed keys and values; add an ordinary backend solely after controlled positive and negative reproduction.

features.label: Provider/HAL sensor routing
features.route: Vendor provider or HAL internal selection

firstBoundary.reason: Static application evidence does not identify a verified application contract for provider/HAL sensor selection.

features.replacementConsequence: Keep provider/HAL assumptions out of the ordinary backend and expose only measured capabilities through device-specific adapters.

features.label: ISP tuning and proprietary imaging controls
features.route: ISP, tuning blobs, native libraries, or firmware services

firstBoundary.reason: No stable application-level contract or causal route-specific tuning interface has been verified.

features.replacementConsequence: Build independent on-device imaging stages and treat proprietary tuning access as unavailable until a lawful, reproducible interface is documented.

features.label: Policy-modified direct endpoint access
features.route: IDs 2 through 5 after package/service/SELinux policy changes

firstBoundary.reason: An ordinary package cannot acquire the required system identity, grants, roles, and allowlist eligibility merely by declaring hidden permissions.

features.replacementConsequence: Implement only as a separately packaged rooted/custom-ROM backend; keep SELinux and CameraService policy as independent gates to verify rather than assumed bypasses.
